**Wave:** 2
**Files:** `alembic/versions/*_create_todo_tasks_table.py`
**Scope:** `alembic/versions/`
**Does:** Writes the one revision, issued by `./scripts/db.sh revision`, with its parent the head
`./scripts/db.sh status` reports (today `a1b2c3d4e5f6`). Its `upgrade()` and `downgrade()` are exactly
the ordered operations of `spec/design/data-model.md` § The revision that creates `todo_tasks`, with the
literal `200` and never the constant, no server default, no data and no backfill. Its mode is
`backward compatible`.
**Depends on:** T-4
**Parallel:** yes, beside every `build-backend` task. Neither imports the other and both build from the
same frozen document, so a service or router case red for the missing table mid-wave is expected.
**Turns green:** T-4's two migration cases.
**Verification:** `./scripts/db.sh migrate` applies it forwards from the current head.
`./scripts/test.sh integration` shows T-4's migration cases passing, and
`test_the_models_and_the_migrations_describe_the_same_schema` passing once T-14's model exists.

T-10's docstring parses. The context's public API names the three, the layer's `__init__.py` carries
its docstring, and one registration line is appended to `app/contexts/__init__.py`.
**Depends on:** T-9, T-10
**Parallel:** its member's first to-do task, since T-15 imports the model. It runs beside T-13, T-17
and every other member.

`tests.fitness.test_context_boundaries::test_every_context_document_has_code_and_every_context_directory_has_a_document`,

part of the text rule. The create shape has no `done`, and the update shape has two optional fields
with `done` read strictly as a boolean. It writes the service's add, read, correct, mark and delete
with the statement shapes of `spec/design/data-model.md` § Two writers on one task: no read before a
write, no upsert, `created_at` from the service's clock on insert only, and the list by `created_at`

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

SAFETY — localhost:5432 on this machine is ANOTHER project's database, not this repository's; never let a script reach it.
The container forge-test1-pythin-react-db-1 holds 0.0.0.0:5432 with the same app/app credentials, and scripts/_lib.sh:62 defaults DATABASE_URL to localhost:${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}. This repository's own dev Postgres is now published on 127.0.0.1:55432 (build-migration moved it after its migrate landed in the other project's database by mistake). The e2e suite empties the database it reaches between scenarios.
So: prefix EVERY ./scripts/start.sh, ./scripts/stop.sh, ./scripts/db.sh, ./scripts/seed.sh, ./scripts/check.sh and ./scripts/test.sh e2e / ui call with POSTGRES_HOST_PORT=55432 (e.g. `POSTGRES_HOST_PORT=55432 ./scripts/test.sh e2e`). If you cannot, do not run them and say so in your closing block. The unit, integration, backend, fitness, tooling and frontend suites start their own test Postgres and are unaffected. — the orchestrator

questions.question: This change's migration landed in the other project's database (forge-test1-pythin-react) by mistake: it created an empty todo_tasks table there and moved that database's version marker to a revision that project doesn't have. What should happen to it?

options.label: Revert it now (Recommended)
options.description: I run `./scripts/db.sh downgrade a1b2c3d4e5f6` against port 5432. It removes only the empty table and index the mistake added, and puts the version marker back where it was.

options.label: I'll fix it there myself
options.description: Nothing more is written to that database from here. You run the downgrade, or your own fix, in that project.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.description: That project's `db.sh migrate` and `db.sh status` will fail on the unknown revision until someone reverts it.

questions.question: For the rest of this change, how should this project stay off port 5432 (the other project's database)?

options.label: Stop the other DB for now (Recommended)
options.description: I run `docker stop forge-test1-pythin-react-db-1` (after the revert, if you chose it). Its data stays in its volume, and `docker start` brings it back later. This project gets port 5432 to itself, and nothing here can reach that database.

options.description: The other project keeps running. I run every database step here, including gates and the fresh-clone check, with POSTGRES_HOST_PORT=55432. It works, but one command without it reaches the other database again.

usage: db.sh <command>

  migrate            Apply every pending migration (alembic upgrade head).
  status             Which revision is applied, which one is the target, and
                     whether anything is left to apply.
  history            The full migration history, newest first.
  revision "message" Autogenerate a migration from the models. Review it before
                     committing -- autogenerate is a first draft, not an answer.
  downgrade <rev>    Move back to a revision. Also takes -1 for one step.
  reset              Drop the database and migrate from scratch. DESTRUCTIVE.
  shell              Open a SQL prompt against the development database.

These target the development Postgres, starting it through docker compose if it
is not up. Postgres is the only engine (spec/design/architecture.md § One engine); with no usable Docker and no
DATABASE_URL of your own they stop and say what to do.

A DATABASE_URL already set in this environment is honoured as it stands -- and
then `reset` and `shell` refuse, because that database is not this script's to
destroy or to reach into through a container it did not start.

93:    downgrade)

106:        [ "${APP_DB_EXTERNAL:-0}" = "1" ] &&
122:        [ "${APP_DB_EXTERNAL:-0}" = "1" ] &&
126:        ensure_db_running
246:ensure_db_running() {
247-    # A database this environment supplied is not ours to start. `resolve_database_url`
248-    # has honoured a pre-set DATABASE_URL since it was written ("never silently
249-    # overridden"), and this function went on composing a container up anyway --
250-    # a contradiction that is invisible while the container happens to be ours and
251-    # fatal the moment it is not.
252-    if [ "${APP_DB_EXTERNAL:-0}" = "1" ]; then
253-        info "the database was supplied by this environment -- nothing to start"
254-        return 0
255-    fi
256-    require_docker
257-    # Three answers, not two: compose that cannot say what is running is not a stopped
258-    # database, and starting one blind over it names the wrong problem.
259-    local running=0
260-    lists_line db docker compose ps --status running --services 2>/dev/null || running=$?
261-    [ "$running" -ne 2 ] ||
262-        die "docker compose could not say which services are running. Run: docker compose ps"
263-    if [ "$running" -ne 0 ]; then
264-        step "Starting Postgres"
265-        docker compose up -d --wait db
266-    fi
267-}
268-
269-#: The development database, resolved and running, ready for alembic.
270-#
271-# Two steps that always go together: decide which Postgres this run means, then

import pathlib

#: file already on the disk.

    """Every untracked path git can see, or `None` if it could not be asked."""

            capture_output=True,
            text=True,

            check=False,

        return None

        return None

## 1. What must become true

A script that starts or reaches "the project's own" development Postgres refuses when the database answering on the configured port is not the container this project started, instead of silently working against another project's database.

## 2. Whose surface this is

The template's `scripts/_lib.sh`: `POSTGRES_URL_DEFAULT` (line 62, `postgresql+psycopg://app:app@localhost:${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}/app`) and `ensure_db_running` (lines 246–267, which asks only whether compose lists `db` as running), used by `db.sh`, `start.sh`, `seed.sh` and `test.sh e2e`; and `docker-compose.yml` line 40 (`${POSTGRES_HOST_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}:5432`) with the fixed `app/app` credentials. Nothing the engine reads is involved; the engine could not fix this.

## 3. Observed

The implement stage, member `build-migration`. Its closing block, verbatim:

```text
./scripts/db.sh migrate -> 0 (it hit the WRONG server, see PROCESS_FAULT)
- PROCESS_FAULT: template: scripts/_lib.sh ensure_db_running only checks that the compose db service is running. forge-test2-react-db-1 was running with bindings 127.0.0.1:5432 but Ports {"5432/tcp":[]}, because another project's container, forge-test1-pythin-react-db-1, holds 0.0.0.0:5432 with the same app/app credentials. So every default db.sh or start.sh call here reaches that project's database. My plain `./scripts/db.sh migrate` applied 5c58af1f8e8a to it and created an empty todo_tasks table there.
```

Confirmed from the orchestrator afterwards:

```text
$ docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Ports}}'
forge-test1-pythin-react-db-1   0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp, [::]:5432->5432/tcp   Up 30 hours
(forge-test2-react-db-1 had been re-created by the worker on 127.0.0.1:55432 by then)
$ DATABASE_URL='postgresql+psycopg://app:app@localhost:5432/app' ./scripts/db.sh status
Rev: 5c58af1f8e8a (head)      <- this instance's revision, in the OTHER project's database
```

With the user's approval the stray revision was reverted there (`db.sh downgrade a1b2c3d4e5f6` against that explicit URL — the other database is back at `a1b2c3d4e5f6`), the other project's container was stopped, and this instance's container was re-created on 5432.

**Worse, and unverified:** this instance's container never had its port, so every earlier script-driven database access of this change went to the other project's database too — including the e2e suites that ran inside the boundary gates at the design and plan closes today (52 scenarios executed at 17:22 UTC), and the e2e suite empties the database it reaches between scenarios. The other project's development data may already have been wiped by this instance; nobody has looked, because reading that database was refused to the worker.

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126 (the engine that ran; not involved).

**Stack:** fastapi-react-postgres

**This instance:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react@26704cc (branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`)

**The template, and the commit this instance came from:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react; the instance's first commit is `6ccb49a Initial commit`, the template commit is not recorded.

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

The template's own comments state the rule and then keep only half of it. `resolve_database_url` (`scripts/_lib.sh` ~148): "A DATABASE_URL somebody set is never silently overridden: it may name a database this script did not create, possibly one holding real data, and substituting the project's own for it would be the worst thing available here." `ensure_db_running` (~247): "a contradiction that is invisible while the container happens to be ours and fatal the moment it is not." The default URL silently names a database this script did not create whenever another process holds the port — the exact hazard those comments name, reached from the other side.

## 5. How it was discovered

Change record CR-2609-823a (tier p3, a new `todo_list` context), stage `implement`, wave 2, skill `build-migration` (the template's), running `./scripts/db.sh migrate` as its skill asks; banked as PROC-46.

## 6. Reproduction

1. On one machine, start the development database of any other project that publishes `0.0.0.0:5432` with user/password `app/app` and database `app` (another instance of this template does exactly that).
2. In an instance of this template, `./scripts/db.sh migrate`. The compose `db` container starts with no published port (5432 is taken), compose still lists it as running, and alembic connects to `localhost:5432` — the other project's database — and migrates it.

Reproduces on the template itself; nothing instance-specific is involved.

## 7. Root cause, so far

CONFIRMED by reading: `ensure_db_running` checks `docker compose ps --status running --services` for `db` and nothing about the port; `POSTGRES_URL_DEFAULT` assumes the configured host port reaches that container; the credentials and database name are the same in every instance, so a cross-connection authenticates.

## 8. Why this instance cannot fix it alone

This instance could patch its own `_lib.sh`, but every instance of the template carries the same default and the same credentials, and this machine alone runs about eighteen Postgres containers from sibling projects. A local patch would leave all of them exposed and diverge this instance from the next template update.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** (a) after starting or finding `db`, ask compose where it actually publishes (`docker compose port db 5432`) and refuse with a sentence naming the conflict when there is no binding or it differs from `POSTGRES_HOST_PORT` — or build the URL from that answer instead of from the configured port; (b) make the default credentials or database name project-specific (derived from the compose project name), so a connection that does reach another project's database fails authentication instead of succeeding.

**Rejected, and why:** documenting "don't run two instances at once" — the machine this was found on runs many, by design; a random host port per instance — breaks the documented `localhost:5432` default every doc and runbook uses.

## 10. Blast radius, inside the template

- **Does every instance of this template have this fault, or only ones that did something?** Every instance on a machine where anything else holds the port.
- **Does the fix change files an existing instance has already diverged from?** `scripts/_lib.sh`, possibly `docker-compose.yml` and `.env` defaults.
- **Does it move anything the ENGINE reads?** No.
- **Which of the template's own tests must change?** The `tests/tooling/` cases for `_lib.sh`, `db.sh` and `start.sh`.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. With another container publishing `0.0.0.0:5432`, `./scripts/db.sh status` in an instance exits non-zero with a sentence naming the port conflict, and runs nothing against `localhost:5432`.
2. With the port free, the default flow is unchanged.

**Proved by:** a new case under the template's `tests/tooling/`.

## 12. What this instance does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: the machine, not the repository: the other project's container `forge-test1-pythin-react-db-1` is stopped while this change runs, and this instance's `db` container is back on 127.0.0.1:5432.
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** The other container is to be started again by its owner when this change is done; with the fix in place the collision will then refuse instead of cross-connecting.

## 13. Not this

Not a request to change the production or CI database set-up, which never shares a host. Not about `DATABASE_URL` supplied from the environment, which is already honoured as it stands.

CONFIRMED by reading `conftest.py` 75–100: the leak set is `after - before` over the whole tree, with no attribution to the pytest process.

Every instance runs the engine's parallel waves in one tree, so every instance meets it; patching this instance's `conftest.py` would diverge from the template's hygiene rule that other instances keep.

**A second face of the same interaction — the template's TypeScript tooling against red-first frontend tests** (banked in CR-2609-823a as PROC-45).

This time it is the typed lint, not the build. While the modules a red-first vitest file imports do not exist, their types resolve to `any`, so `@typescript-eslint` rules that need types cannot see what the test does. The error surfaces only after the implementation lands — in the implementers' wave, where no member may edit a test.

`build-frontend`'s closing block (wave 2), verbatim:

```text
- STATUS: TEST_DISPUTED
./scripts/lint.sh -> 1 (only 5 eslint errors, all in a test file, see DISPUTED_TEST; ruff, mypy, tsc OK)
- PROCESS_FAULT: The typed lint of the wave-1 vitest files cannot see their real types until wave 2 creates the modules they import (the unresolved types are `any`). So a test-file lint error (await-thenable) passes the RED proof and first surfaces in wave 2, where no member may edit tests.
- DISPUTED_TEST: frontend/src/contexts/todo_list/hooks/useTodoTasks.test.tsx, lines 185, 252, 259, 272 and 280. `await act(() => result.current.<mutation>.mutate(...))` awaits the void that TanStack's `mutate` returns. @typescript-eslint/await-thenable fails ./scripts/lint.sh (--max-warnings 0), and so check.sh.
```

The engine routes it correctly (a disputed test goes back to its author), at the price of one more dispatch. What the template could add: in `build-tests-frontend`'s guidance, the idiom that is correct whatever the types turn out to be — `await act(async () => { … })`, never `await` on a call whose return type the test cannot see yet — and/or a lint pass over test files at the end of the test-author wave that reports type-dependent rules as "unverifiable until the modules exist" rather than silently green.

    --matrix) shift; require_python_floor; exec "$SDD_PYTHON" "$SDD_ENGINE/traceability.py" --all --matrix "$@" ;;
    # `--executed <report>` reaches traceability.py through here too: the mode passes its
    # flags on unchanged, so the table can be read against a run as well as against the text.
esac

input.content:
## 1. What must become true

A gate run's requirement-traceability step judges which citing tests *ran* from that same run, so the first gate after a change's tests appear does not report every requirement uncovered.

## 2. The coupling surface

`bin/sdd-specs` (lines 150–158, which pass `--executed "$REPO_ROOT/.sdd/reports/last-gate.json"` to `traceability.py`), `skills/_shared/sdd/gate.py` (`run --out`), and every profile whose specs step includes traceability — `fast`, `boundary`, `full`.

## 3. Observed

Implement stage, after the implementation wave; every suite green. `sdd-engine gate run --profile fast --json --out .sdd/reports/fast.json` (started 2026-09-24T19:21:08Z), verbatim:

```text
Check: OK
==> Requirement traceability
CR-2609-823a: 11 declared, 0 referenced, 1 manual
  UNCOVERED  CR-2609-823a/R-1
  ... (R-2 to R-10 the same)
CR-2609-9b1e: 7 declared, 7 referenced, 0 manual
Failed gates:
  - Requirement traceability
  - Diff-scoped gates
```

The same tree, the same minute:

```text
$ sdd-engine traceability --cr CR-2609-823a
CR-2609-823a: 11 declared, 10 referenced, 1 manual
$ sdd-engine traceability --cr CR-2609-823a --executed .sdd/reports/last-gate.json
CR-2609-823a: 11 declared, 0 referenced, 1 manual
$ jq -r '[.profile, .started_at] | @tsv' .sdd/reports/last-gate.json
boundary   2026-09-24T16:46:28Z      <- the plan close, before any test of this change existed
```

Every gate run of this session passed `--out` (two RED proofs, the fast gate), and `gate run --out X` writes only `X`, so `last-gate.json` stayed at 16:46 for three hours while the tests were written, observed red and turned green.

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126 — read from the path the engine loads from (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/`).

**Stack:** fastapi-react-postgres

**Level:** instance

**Repository, and its commit:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react@26704cc (plus the TD-3 checkpoint after it)

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

`traceability.py`'s own docstring: "A citation is not a run, and `--executed` is where the difference is made" — the axis exists to ask whether the citing tests ran. A report from before the tests existed answers "no" for every one of them, which is not a measurement of the run being judged. The consequence reaches `loop close`: its boundary gate's specs step reads the same stale file, so the stage cannot close green on its first gate after the tests appear.

## 5. How it was discovered

jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react, branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`, change record CR-2609-823a (tier p3), stage `implement`, the row-33 gate after wave 2, orchestrator `/forge:sdd`.

## 6. Reproduction

1. Have `.sdd/reports/last-gate.json` from a run before a change's tests existed (any earlier stage close).
2. Write tests citing the change's requirements; run gates only with `--out` (the RED proof recipe does).
3. `sdd-engine gate run --profile fast --json --out x.json` — traceability: "0 referenced", every requirement UNCOVERED, although the run's own suites executed and passed the citing tests.

## 7. Root cause, so far

CONFIRMED by reading `bin/sdd-specs` 150–158: the executed axis is always the file `last-gate.json` as it stands when the specs step starts — i.e. the previous run's record, never the current one — and `gate run --out` does not refresh that file.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

`sdd-specs`, `gate.py` and `traceability.py` are the engine's. This level can only arrange for `last-gate.json` to hold a recent record before the close — which it did by running `sdd-engine gate run --profile unit --json` without `--out`.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** have `gate.py` hand the specs step the executed lists of the suites it has just run in this run (write the suites' half of the record first, pass `--executed <that>`), falling back to `last-gate.json` only when the run has no suites of its own; and/or make `gate run --out X` also refresh `last-gate.json`, or print which report the executed axis was read from and its timestamp.

**Rejected, and why:** dropping the executed axis — it exists for a measured reason (a marker on a skipped test); asking orchestrators to run an extra gate without `--out` — a ritual that nobody will remember.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** All.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** No.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No.
- **Which existing tests must change?** The engine's gate/traceability tests.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. With a `last-gate.json` older than a change's tests, `sdd-engine gate run --profile fast --json --out x.json` over a tree whose citing tests pass reports the change's requirements as referenced.
2. The traceability line in a gate's output names the report its executed axis came from.

**Proved by:** a new case beside the engine's gate and traceability tests.

## 12. What this repository does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: this session ran `sdd-engine gate run --profile unit --json` (no `--out`) before `loop close`, so `last-gate.json` holds a record that executed the new tests.
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** No — it leaves nothing behind.

## 13. Not this

Not about the delivery-conditioned `change-record` asserts in the `fast` profile (filed separately).

sdd-engine change_state ask-question --cr <CR> --from-json <file.json>

[
  {
    "question": "Can a task exist with nobody assigned to it?",
    "allow_free_text": true,
    "blocks": ["COH-design-3"],
    "blocking": false,
    "options": [
      {"key": "A", "label": "Yes, nobody assigned means 'up for grabs'",
       "recommended": true,  "consequence": "A task can be opened before anyone knows who will do it"},
      {"key": "B", "label": "No, a person is required",
       "recommended": false, "consequence": "Nobody will record a task 'for later'"}
    ]
  }
]

Exactly one option has `recommended: true` and stands first -- a panel with no recommendation
pushes onto the user the analysis that was the process's job.

`qid` is optional and normally left out: the record allocates the next free `Q-n` per item,
in array order, and prints them back as `qids`. You could not compute it in any case, since
the ids in use are in `change.json` and `action_log.jsonl` and both are out of bounds here.
Asking the same question again while it is still open returns the id it already has.

`blocks` names what waits for the answer -- coherence findings, repair tasks, the members
this decides. Leave it out and the question holds the whole stage, which is what a question
with no `blocks` has always done. Name ids and it holds those and nothing else: the rest of
the pass moves while the person thinks. It can never hold nothing -- the stage's gate still
refuses to close over a question raised in it that is still open.

`blocking` is about WHEN it is asked, not what it holds: true sends it out at once instead
of waiting for the wave in the air to land. Justify it in the question's own text.
The contract for both: skills/_shared/question-policy.md.

### COH-implement-6 — Were the reds that ran ahead of the code declared on a task, or signed off at the design close?

- **kind:** contradiction
- **severity:** minor
- **decision_mode:** HITL
- **auto_basis:**
- **ambiguity_source:** spec/design/testing.md § CR-2609-823a, the to-do list
- **artifacts:** tasks.md, spec/design/testing.md, spec/contexts/todo_list.md

**What each says.** The specification says every red was declared on a task:
- `spec/design/testing.md` § CR-2609-823a, "Existing detectors that go red on the way" (:958-960):
  "each is declared on the task whose product closes it".
- Its third bullet (:979-982) says the on-disk case is "declared on build-tests-e2e's task".
- `spec/contexts/todo_list.md`:30-32: "the plan declares
  `test_every_screen_and_feature_a_context_names_is_on_disk` red on the task that writes the file.
  The declaration expires when that task writes the file".

`tasks.md` did otherwise:
- T-11 says the on-disk case "has been red since … (`Q-19`, signed off at the design close,
  `Q-24`), and the implement baseline carries it … It is not declared".
- T-14 carries the context-boundaries case the same way.
- § What can go in parallel: "The `Turns green:` cases carried from the design close … are
  baseline reds, not declarations."
- The seed-file cases were declared on T-10 and T-4, the tasks that turned them red, and T-17
  closed them.

The session trace records the sign-off: `[18:49] stage_closed: closed design, opened plan
(boundary -> RED; accepted RED: Application check, Suite fitness: structural at the design
boundary`, right after `Q-24 -> A`.

**Why they cannot both be true.** The specification says each red was declared on the task that
closes it. The plan and the record tell a different story: two reds were accepted by name at the
design boundary and carried as a baseline, and the rest were declared on the task that turned
them red. The merged specification can keep only one account.

A red that already stood at the design close could not be declared on a task of a plan not yet
written, before the run that showed it (constitution Article X). That is why `Q-24` accepted it,
following the pattern COH-design-10 set for `./scripts/contracts.sh`. Graded minor.

**What settles it.** Nothing on the ladder. `Q-24` is recorded only in the change record, so this
is HITL by iron rule 2. The human step is to confirm the account; it is not a new question.

reconcile-spec in `todo_list.md`.

**Q-25**: When someone opens the to-do list with the link at the top of the page, should it always fetch the latest list, or may it show the copy it fetched up to 30 seconds earlier? - **A: Always fetch the latest** (the recommendation). Skutek: The to-do list asks for the current list every time it is opened; the guestbook is left as it is, and the acceptance script reloads the page before its step 14.
- **B: Up to 30 seconds old is fine**. Skutek: The screen documents say that opening by the link may show the list as it was up to 30 seconds ago; the acceptance script reloads the page before its step 14.

**Q-26**: The rules page for the project's sample data (golden-set/README.md) now has five out-of-date sentences: it still describes only the guestbook's sample files, not the to-do list's. No step of this change is allowed to edit that page — it has no owner in the project's setup, already reported to the template as issue #92. What should happen?

- **A: Fix it in a follow-up** (the recommendation). Skutek: This change's pull request names the five sentences, and a small documentation-only pull request right after it corrects them with the wording already prepared; the page is out of date only between the two merges.
- **B: Only note it in the pull request**. Skutek: The five sentences are named in the pull request and left to the template's issue #92; the page stays out of date until someone picks that up.

**Q-27**: At the end of the design stage you approved closing it with known failing checks (your answer to Q-24). Two of those failures were then carried into this stage and fixed by the new code, instead of being declared against a specific task as the test design document describes. Should the design documents be corrected to record what actually happened?
- wstrzymuje: COH-implement-6
- **A: Yes, record what happened** (the recommendation). Skutek: The specification step rewrites those sentences in the test design and the to-do list description to say the two failures were signed off at the design close (Q-24) and fixed in this stage; nothing in the product changes.
- **B: No, leave the documents**. Skutek: The documents keep describing a declaration that never happened, so the merged specification and the change's record disagree.

Parsed rather than typed twice. A boundary the orchestrator retypes into a
    verb is a boundary that can disagree with the document a human approved, and
    then the check runs against something nobody agreed to.

    The source moved with the design itself. There is no `design.md` any more --
    the design edits `spec/`, and what is change-scoped is the fragment each author
    leaves behind. `design/delta/architecture.md` owns the section, because deciding
    the write sets IS that author's job; the other fragments are read after it so a
    change whose tier runs no architecture step can still declare a boundary.
    """
    sources = _boundary_sources(change_dir)
    if not sources:
        raise StateError(
            f"{_display(change_dir / DESIGN_DELTA_DIR)} holds no fragment. The boundary is "
            "declared under 'This change owns' in a design delta fragment and read from "
            "there; there is nothing to read yet."
        )

    paths: list[str] = []
    for source in sources:
        if scaffold.is_template(source):
            continue
        inside = False
        for line in source.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if _OWNS_HEADING.match(line):
                inside = True
                continue
            if inside and _NEXT_HEADING.match(line):
                inside = False
                continue
            if inside and (match := _OWNS_ROW.match(line)):
                candidate = match.group("path").strip()
                # The template's own placeholder row is not a declaration.
                if candidate and not candidate.startswith("<"):
                    paths.append(candidate)

    if not paths:
        named = ", ".join(_display(source) for source in sources)
        raise StateError(
            "no design delta fragment declares a path under 'This change owns' "
            f"({named}). A change that will not say what it owns cannot be told it went "
            "outside -- which is the whole point of the section."
        )
    return sorted(dict.fromkeys(paths))

2084	case is renamed. Each file goes to the author whose tree holds it: build-tests-unit for

### COH-implement-4 — Do the structural tests still say there is one context, one table and one revision?

- **kind:** contradiction
- **severity:** minor
- **decision_mode:** AUTO
- **auto_basis:** spec/constitution.md § Article I — The specification is the source of truth
- **ambiguity_source:** spec/design/testing.md § Four file sets, disjoint
- **artifacts:** spec/design/testing.md, tests/fitness/test_context_declarations.py, tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py, tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py, tests/fitness/test_migration_safety.py, tests/integration/test_migrations.py

**What each says.** `spec/design/testing.md` § Fitness functions was corrected at design:
- :200-201: `test_context_boundaries.py` and `test_context_declarations.py` "were vacuously true
  while there was one context", and the sweeps now read real headers.
- :217: for `test_data_invariants.py`, "`todo_tasks` made them real".
- :211: for `test_migration_safety.py`, "each of the two revisions".

The tests' docstrings still state the old facts, in the present tense:
- `tests/fitness/test_context_declarations.py`:31: "Most of these are **vacuously true today** --
  there is one context". :299: "Vacuously true while there is one context, and it says so."
- `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py`:28: "**Every rule here is vacuously true today**:
  there is one context". :145: "Vacuously true with one context". :213: "With one context
  nothing can cross".
- `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py`:16-18: "vacuously true today … the guest book is one
  table". :92: "Vacuously true while the guest book is the only table".
- `tests/fitness/test_migration_safety.py`:27: "the one revision here creates a table and its
  index together".
- `tests/integration/test_migrations.py`:128: "`BR-04` is read on every load of the only screen".
  This stage edited that file (T-4).

Command: `grep -rn "vacuously true today\|Vacuously true with one context\|Vacuously true while
there is one context\|With one context nothing\|one revision here\|the only screen\|only table"
tests/fitness/*.py tests/integration/test_migrations.py
frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx`. It printed every line cited here and in
COH-implement-5.

**Why they cannot both be true.** The specification says these sweeps now judge real material. The
tests' own docstrings say they are vacuous. Article IX makes the module docstring the place where a
check's intent is kept. A reader who trusts it will take a red from these sweeps for a synthetic
known positive, not a real breach. Graded minor: no assertion is affected.

**What settles it.** `spec/constitution.md` § Article I: "Code contradicting `spec/` is either a
defect in the code or a change not applied to the specification." The specification changed at
design, so the code's text is the defect.

**Resolution.** The docstrings say what `testing.md` says. Text only: no assertion changes and no
case is renamed. Each file goes to the author whose tree holds it: build-tests-unit for
`tests/fitness/`, build-tests-integration for `test_migrations.py`.

Ready patch:
- `test_context_declarations.py`:31-32. Replace "Most of these are **vacuously true today** --
  there is one context, and it borders on nothing." with "Most of these were **vacuously true**
  while there was one context bordering on nothing; since `CR-2609-823a` two contexts declare each
  other, and the sweeps read real headers."
- `test_context_declarations.py`:299. Replace "Vacuously true while there is one context, and it
  says so." with "Vacuously true while there was one context; since `CR-2609-823a` it reads two
  real neighbours."
- `test_context_boundaries.py`:28-29. Replace "**Every rule here is vacuously true today**: there
  is one context, so no import can cross a boundary that does not exist." with "**Every rule here
  was vacuously true** while there was one context, since no import could cross a boundary that
  did not exist; since `CR-2609-823a` there are two."
- `test_context_boundaries.py`:145. Replace "Vacuously true with one context; the detector is
  proved below." with "Real since `CR-2609-823a` brought a second context; the detector is proved
  below."
- `test_context_boundaries.py`:213-214. Replace "This is where the rule lives today. With one
  context nothing can cross, so the sweeps above would pass over a reader that always answered
  None." with "This is where the rule lived while there was one context: nothing could cross, so
  the sweeps above would have passed over a reader that always answered None."
- `test_data_invariants.py`:16-18. Replace "**Two of these are vacuously true today and that is
  said out loud**" with "**Two of these were vacuously true while the guest book was the only
  table, and that was said out loud**". Replace "the guest book is one table, so nothing can
  mirror it and nothing can copy from it." with "the guest book was one table, so nothing could
  mirror it and nothing could copy from it; `todo_tasks` made them real."
- `test_data_invariants.py`:92. Replace "Vacuously true while the guest book is the only table,
  and that is fine:" with "Vacuously true while the guest book was the only table:".
- `test_migration_safety.py`:27. Replace "the one revision here creates a table and its index
  together" with "each of the two revisions here creates its table and its index together".
- `test_migrations.py`:128. Replace "read on every load of the only screen" with "read on every
  load of the guestbook's screen".

**What was ambiguous.** `testing.md` § Four file sets lists every edit a test author makes to an
existing test, and it names none of these five files. Yet § Fitness functions, in the same
document, was corrected for exactly the facts they state; COH-design-17 corrected the
migration-safety row. `requirements.md` § Impact analysis even predicted that two of them "stop
being vacuously true". The specification moved, and no write set carried the move into the
tests' prose.

**What was not found.** No assertion rests on these sentences, and every known positive still runs.
Two other passages are dated records of an incident and are true as history:
`tests/fitness/test_alembic_env_metadata.py`:8 and `tests/fitness/test_migration_safety.py`:94.

### COH-implement-5 — Does the guestbook screen still call itself the only screen?

- **kind:** contradiction
- **severity:** minor
- **decision_mode:** AUTO
- **auto_basis:** spec/constitution.md § Article I — The specification is the source of truth
- **ambiguity_source:** spec/design/architecture.md § The files
- **artifacts:** frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx, spec/design/ui/system-states.md

**What each says.** `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx`:30: "`S-01` -- the
only screen in this application." `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column: "The
application has two screens, the guestbook and the to-do list".

Two documents freeze the guestbook's frontend:
- `spec/design/architecture.md` § The files, row for the three guestbook modules: "nothing else
  about the guestbook moves".
- `design/delta/architecture.md` § What this change does not move: "Its frontend changes by three
  import paths and nothing else".

`GuestbookPage.tsx` is not one of the three modules. T-22 made the frame's docstrings stop saying
there is one screen, but it did not reach this one.

**Why they cannot both be true.** A module docstring states a fact that the specification now
contradicts. It sits in the first file a reader opens for the guestbook's screen, and Article IX
says module docstrings cite the specification. The claim is not on screen, so `R-5` clause 4 is
not broken. Graded minor.

**What settles it.** `spec/constitution.md` § Article I, as for COH-implement-4.

**Resolution.** One line in `GuestbookPage.tsx`, taken as a behaviour-neutral exception to the
freeze.

Ready patch, `GuestbookPage.tsx`:30. Replace "`S-01` -- the only screen in this application." with
"`S-01` -- the guestbook's screen, one of this application's two
(`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column)."

**What was ambiguous.** `architecture.md` § The files freezes the guestbook's frontend for its
behaviour. It makes no exception for the file's prose, which the second screen made false.

**What was not found.** The same freeze is why `PageFrame.tsx` carries the guestbook's footer as
the default of `footer`, which build-frontend reported. Each screen still shows its own sentence
and the not-found page shows none, as `system-states.md` § Regions requires. So that is a debt,
not a contradiction. If the file is opened for this line, the footer can move into it too.

## 1. What must become true

When a later stage's convergence settles a finding by a code edit to a path outside the recorded boundary, the process has a named way to grow the boundary by exactly that path — instead of the edit being refused by the worker's verify and the orchestrator inventing a route.

## 2. The coupling surface

`change_state set-boundary --from-design` (it reads "## This change owns" from every design delta fragment, `design/delta/architecture.md` first), `skill_gate.py`'s boundary check in a worker's verify, and `review-converge`'s guidance on its fragment.

## 3. Observed

Implement stage, coherence pass 7. `COH-implement-5` (AUTO, constitution Art. I) resolved that one module-docstring line of `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx` changes, and `review-converge` reconciled it by adding a row for that file to `spec/design/architecture.md` § The files. The recorded boundary did not list the file, and nothing re-derives it from the live `architecture.md`. The reconciler's closing block, verbatim:

```text
- ASSUMPTIONS: ... RISK for the orchestrator: frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx is not in design/delta/architecture.md § This change owns, which the boundary is recorded from. Unless the boundary is extended, build-frontend's COH-implement-5 edit may be refused.
```

`skill_gate.py` (worker verify) refuses a write outside the boundary ("A path satisfies the first and violates the second exactly where scope grows without anybody deciding it did"), and `set-boundary` takes only `--from-design`. The route this session found: a second `review-converge` dispatch (todo TD-4) that added a hand-made "## This change owns" section with the one row to its own fragment `design/delta/converge.md`, then `set-boundary --from-design`:

```text
OK  boundary=43  from_design=35  from_reconciliation=8
```

The second dispatch's closing block, verbatim:

```text
- PROCESS_FAULT: When design-architecture's owns table is the only one, the boundary has no route to grow by a path that a later-stage convergence edit to spec/design/architecture.md § The files adds. COH-implement-5 added a GuestbookPage.tsx row there, but the boundary is read from the design delta fragments alone, so the gap only showed as a refused write (TD-4) and needed a hand-made owns section in converge.md.
```

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126 — read from the path the engine loads from (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/`).

**Stack:** fastapi-react-postgres

**Level:** instance

**Repository, and its commit:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react (branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`, the TD-4 checkpoint)

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

`set-boundary`'s own help: "the only source there is -- retyping it lets it disagree with the approved document". A convergence round that settles a finding by editing code outside the boundary is a decided scope growth (the finding names its auto basis), yet no skill says where that decision is declared so the boundary can follow it; `review-converge` writes `converge.md` but nothing tells it to add an owns row for a path its reconciliation makes some builder edit.

## 5. How it was discovered

Change record CR-2609-823a (tier p3), stage `implement`, after coherence pass 7 and its convergence; banked as PROC-53.

## 6. Reproduction

1. At implement, a coherence finding resolves (auto or by a human) that a file outside the recorded boundary changes; `review-converge` reconciles the live spec.
2. Dispatch the owning builder for the edit: its `verify` refuses the path as outside the boundary; `set-boundary --from-design` does not add it, because no design fragment's owns table names it.

## 7. Root cause, so far

CONFIRMED by reading `change_state.py` (`boundary_from_design`, `_boundary_sources`): the boundary is only ever the union of the fragments' owns tables; no reconciliation-time path adds to it, and `review-converge`'s skill does not ask for an owns row.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The boundary verbs, the worker verify and the reconciler's skill are the engine's.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** have `review-converge` write an owns row in its own fragment for every path outside the boundary that a resolution it reconciles requires a builder to edit (with the finding id as the reason), and have `loop back` for `review-converge` re-run `set-boundary --from-design` and print the paths it added — so the growth is declared by the step that decided it and visible in the record.

**Rejected, and why:** a `set-boundary --add <path>` verb for the orchestrator — retyped paths are what the verb's help warns against; refusing such findings — they are legitimate Art. I corrections.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** All.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** No.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No.
- **Which existing tests must change?** `test_sdd_boundary.py` cases for reconciliation-time growth.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. A resolved finding whose resolution names a path outside the boundary, reconciled by `review-converge`, leaves an owns row for that path in `converge.md`, and `loop back --member review-converge` reports the boundary grew by it.
2. The builder dispatched for that path passes its verify.

**Proved by:** new cases beside `test_sdd_boundary.py`.

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/design/delta/converge.md` § This change owns (one row, added by a scoped `review-converge` dispatch).
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** No — the row is a true declaration of what the change owns.

## 13. Not this

Not a request to let builders write outside the boundary, nor to loosen the boundary check.

content.thinking: Found that cached plugin versions sort lexicographically rather than numerically, so a worker taking the "last" match could load a contract dozens of versions out of date—more serious than a minor lookup issue. I'll file this with that detail included.

input.command:
cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jaroslawwasowski-Projects-Forge-forge-test2-react/76720804-74cc-4a32-b0f2-3b64b73aa9dd/scratchpad/proc-55-body.md <<'EOF'
## 1. What must become true

A worker running a template's own skill reads the worker contract (and `process-failure.md`, `verification.md`) of the plugin version that is actually running, because its preflight brief prints their resolved local paths.

## 2. The coupling surface

The worker preflight brief (`sdd-skill <skill> preflight`) and the template skills under a project's `.claude/skills/` (the `build-*` members), which cite `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/worker-contract.md`, a variable the harness expands only inside plugin skills.

## 3. Observed

Implement stage, a `build-frontend` dispatch (a template skill). Its closing block, verbatim:

```text
- PROCESS_FAULT: The skill's iron rules cite `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/worker-contract.md`, but the preflight brief prints no expanded local path for it, so the worker has to search the plugin cache (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.76/...`) to read the contract it is bound by. Cost: one discovery call.
```

The session was running plugin **0.1.126**. The cache holds many versions, and a lexical sort puts `0.1.76` after `0.1.126`:

```text
$ ls -d ~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/*/ | tail -5
.../forge/0.1.62/
.../forge/0.1.67/
.../forge/0.1.68/
.../forge/0.1.74/
.../forge/0.1.76/
$ grep -n 'CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT' .claude/skills/build-platform/SKILL.md | head -1
40:The contract of every SDD worker — fourteen rules and the closing block you end your answer with: [`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/worker-contract.md`](https://github.com/.../worker-contract.md). It binds you in full; ...
```

So a worker that resolves the variable by searching the cache can end up bound by a contract fifty releases old, silently.

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126 — read from the path the running engine loads from.

**Stack:** fastapi-react-postgres

**Level:** instance

**Repository, and its commit:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react (branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`)

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

The skills say the contract "binds you in full"; a binding document has to be the running version's. Plugin skills get `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` expanded by the harness (the orchestrator's own SKILL.md shows `/…/forge/0.1.126/skills/_shared/…`); template skills in `.claude/skills/` do not, and nothing in the preflight fills the gap.

## 5. How it was discovered

Change record CR-2609-823a (tier p3), stage `implement`, a scoped `build-frontend` dispatch (todo TD-7), orchestrator `/forge:sdd`; banked as PROC-55.

## 6. Reproduction

1. In an instance of a template whose `build-*` skills cite `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/worker-contract.md`, with several plugin versions in the cache.
2. `sdd-skill build-frontend preflight` — no line names the contract's local path; the worker must search the cache.

## 7. Root cause, so far

CONFIRMED that the variable is unexpanded in the template skill text (the grep above) and that the cache sorts `0.1.76` last. HYPOTHESIS that the preflight omits the path for template skills only (plugin-skill preflights were not compared).

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The preflight brief is the engine's, and only the engine knows its own root at run time; a template cannot write the path into its skills, and an instance even less.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** have every worker preflight print a `CONTRACT:` line with the resolved paths of `worker-contract.md`, `process-failure.md` and `verification.md` from the running plugin root (and optionally the version), so a template skill can say "read the contract your preflight names".

**Rejected, and why:** telling templates to link GitHub `main` only — needs network and may be ahead of the running version; pruning old cache versions — the harness's cache, not the engine's, and a sort-order trap still remains.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** Every template with its own skills.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes; the line is additive.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** No.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No.
- **Which existing tests must change?** Preflight-brief tests.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. `sdd-skill build-frontend preflight` in an instance prints the absolute paths of the three shared documents under the running plugin's root.

**Proved by:** a preflight-brief case in the engine's tests.

## 12. What this repository does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [ ] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at:
- [x] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit (the worker found a copy; which version it read is not known)

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** None was made.

## 13. Not this

Not about the content of the worker contract, nor about the harness's cache retention.

tasks as they are stored at that moment, other people's changes of the last few seconds included.

the guestbook and back by the header links within 30 seconds and shows the tick.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jaroslawwasowski/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/skills/sdd-retro

# SDD Retro

<prerequisites>
## PREREQUISITES

### Stage 1 — Automated checks

    sdd-skill sdd-retro scripts/retro_capture.py preflight

**Read what it prints. Do not pipe it, do not truncate it, do not write a filter for it.**
It prints finished text now, precisely so there is nothing to parse — the JSON envelope it
used to print was run through `head -60` and through two hand-written `python3 -c` filters in
session `0d433f45`, which is how the size ratchet `MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES` came to exist.

This is the only command called a preflight. `preflight.py` beside this file is the shared
conversational brief every skill has; the line above is the one that matters here, because it
seeds the summary and reports the size.

### Stage 2 — Preparation

None. **Do not open the transcript files** — they are megabytes of JSONL, you already lived
the session they record, and pulling them into context is the one action that can make this
skill cost more than everything it archives.

**Nothing in the pipeline depends on this skill, and nothing should** -- but since
2026-09-21 an ending no longer depends on it either. The `SessionEnd` hook archives the
bytes of every session, so the question this skill answers has narrowed to the one only
this session can answer: what it *meant*. The archive is no longer at risk if you are
interrupted; the meaning still is.

**And do not go looking for numbers either.** This skill produces no measurements at all.
Tokens, tool mix, rule breaches and the rest are computed once, for *every* session of this
repository, when the corpus is collected (`sdd-retro dump`) — where they cost no
context and cover far more than this one run. What only you have is the meaning.
</prerequisites>

<iron_rules>
## IRON RULES

1. **The archive is the product.** This skill captures raw material for an analysis somebody
   else performs later, across many sessions. Evidence you improved is evidence you destroyed.
2. **Never open a `.jsonl`, and never call a history tool.** Not the file, not
   `session_audit.py`, not `mcp__sdd-history__*`, not `mcp__claude-history__*`. The script
   copies the transcript; you never read it back. A summary written by re-reading the
   transcript is a summary of what you can still fit in context, which is the last third of
   the session — and an audit assembled from counters is an audit of what a counter can see.
   **Both documents come from the conversation you are in.** That is the only place holding
   why you chose this route, what you looked for and did not find, and where you turned back;
   none of it is in the record, and no tool can recover it once this context is gone.
3. **Never dispatch a subagent.** Two reasons, and either alone is enough: a subagent writes
   into `subagents/` inside the very tree being copied, so the capture would race its own
   evidence; and a fresh context has no session to audit, so the judgement it returned would
   be about nothing.
4. **`summary.md` proposes nothing. `audit.md` judges.** The witness records what happened
   and never what should have happened instead; the judge says plainly what went wrong. Two
   files because the rules are opposite: one must stay an unimproved sample, the other must
   be blunt. Never let either leak into the other.
5. **A claim is not evidence, including your own.** "The tests pass" is a claim; the exit code
   of `./scripts/check.sh` is evidence. Where you cannot produce evidence, write the claim
   down as unverified rather than softening it into probably true.
6. **Look for the bent rule, not the broken one.** A rule broken outright fails a gate. A rule
   *bent* — a requirement written vaguer so it was easier to satisfy, a test asserting less
   than the requirement it cites, a delta `**Why:**` that restates the change — passes
   everything, and is the whole reason this half of the skill exists.
7. **A root cause is a hypothesis until you have read the code.** When a finding blames a
   deterministic failure — a `fail()` in a script, a validator, a preflight, a gate — and you
   have not read that code in this session, write "probably, to be confirmed in
   `file.py`" and name the file. A confidently wrong cause routes the repair at the wrong
   thing while looking exactly like a repair.
8. **Fix nothing, and file nothing.** Not the code, not the skills, not the rules, and not an
   issue against any of them. Repair is a separate round, run from
   `/Users/jaroslawwasowski/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/retro-prompts/`. A skill that finds and fixes is a skill grading its own work,
   and one that finds and files is the same skill with a URL. What you DO owe a process
   finding is the question of whether anybody else will ever see it: for each bent rule, say
   whether it was filed and where, or that it was not. You are the backstop for
   `/Users/jaroslawwasowski/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/skills/_shared/process-failure.md`, not its mechanism — the session files, and you
   record what the session did.
9. **Commit with the verb, never by hand.** `commit` stages the archive and refuses anything
   else. `CR-2608-9373` carries a committed *unfilled* summary with no transcript and no
   manifest, swept in by `git add spec/changes/<CR>/` — five prose steps failed once already.
10. **Push, and let the project say whether to ask.** The session ends on the remote,
    because an archive on one laptop is one disk failure from gone and every reader of the
    corpus reads what was pushed. Whether a question precedes it is `boundary.push` in
    `.specconf/process.json`: `ask` puts it to the user with the megabytes and the
    personal-data counts above it; `auto` pushes and then says what it did. Read the
    setting, never guess it — `plan-push` prints it. Decision of 2026-08-22 made this a
    push at all; the setting was added when the retro became a beat of every stage
    boundary, because a question asked eight times per change is a question nobody reads.
11. **An empty section is data.** A section with nothing in it says "this did not happen". A
    section you fill by inventing contaminates the count it feeds.
</iron_rules>

<role>
## ROLE

You are the **archivist and the cold reviewer** of the session you are in — in that order,
and the order matters: archive first, judge second, because the judgement must not be able to
edit the evidence it is about.

**Expertise:**
- Writing a summary that is still legible as the fortieth row of a table
- Telling what happened from what you concluded about what happened
- Knowing which facts are already measured and which only you can supply

**Mindset:**
- **The transcript records what was done; you record why it changed.** A person changing their
  mind mid-sentence leaves no marker anywhere in the JSONL. That is your section.
- **You are the one reader who cannot judge whether the documents were clear**, because you
  were here. Ask what a person who was not here would have made of them.
- **Praise is cheap and useless.** So is a manufactured problem. Be genuinely critical, and do
  not invent a finding to look thorough.
- **Stable headings beat good prose.** Both documents will be read by a script before they are
  read by a person.
</role>

<mandatory_todowrite>
## MANDATORY TODOWRITE

Your phases, in order — hold them as a todo list:

```
Phase 1: Preflight
Phase 2: Capture
Phase 3: Audit
Phase 4: Write the summary
Phase 5: Verify and commit
Phase 6: Ask, then push
```

One `in_progress` at a time, closed the moment the phase ends rather than in one burst
at the finish: a list ticked off at the end records that you were here, not where you got
to. If your runtime offers no todo tool, the phases are still your list — report them in
the closing block and spend no turn looking for a workaround.
</mandatory_todowrite>

<context>
## PURPOSE & CONTEXT

**Context.** The SDD process is judged from its own traces, and for a long time nothing kept
them: transcripts expire quietly under `~/.claude/projects/` on Claude Code's own schedule.
Two skills used to split this job — one archived and was forbidden to think, one thought and
was never once invoked in 76 sessions, leaving no artefact anywhere. Half of its rubric
restated the summary's own sections. They are one skill now.

**Goal.** One directory per session inside the change record: the raw transcript, a structured
summary, an audit written from the conversation, and an empty `feedback.md` waiting for
the user — committed, so a question asked in six months has three independent sentences about
the same run behind it. Three, because that is the smallest number that shows what the agent
does not know about itself: the summary says what happened, the audit says how the agent
judges it, and the feedback says how the person who sat through it judges it.

**What this skill catches:**
- A session whose only record was a context that got cleared
- A decision taken in conversation and written down nowhere else
- The instruction sentence somebody hesitated at, which no script can reconstruct
- A claim this session made that its own state does not support
- A rule bent rather than broken, which every gate passed
</context>

<input_parsing>
## INPUT PARSING

Nothing is parsed from the sentence. Every fact is derived.

| What | From |
|---|---|
| Which session | `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, via `/Users/jaroslawwasowski/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/skills/_shared/sdd/session_id.py` |
| Which change | the git branch, via `/Users/jaroslawwasowski/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/skills/_shared/sdd/focus.py` |

| What the user noticed | `retro/notes/<data>.md`, printed by `audit` |
| What happened and what it meant | **you, from the conversation you are in** |
| What it cost, in numbers | nowhere here — `sdd-retro dump`, later, for every session |

Optional: `--session <id>` archives an earlier session into the current change.

**This skill runs on the change branch, before the merge.** It reads the change from the
branch, so on the trunk there is nothing to archive into.

**It is the last step of every session, not only of the last one.** A stage boundary tells
the user to open a new window, so a boundary *is* a session's end — and `close_stage.py`
prints this skill as beat 2 of the sequence it numbers. Which boundaries run it is

<quick_reference>

</quick_reference>

<common_rationalizations>
## COMMON RATIONALIZATIONS

| Excuse | Reality |
|---|---|
| "I will skim the transcript to write a better summary" | It is megabytes of JSONL and you lived the session. Skimming gets you the last third and costs more than the archive is worth. |
| "The summary looks thin, I will add some analysis" | Analysis has its own file. A thin summary of a thin session is a correct summary. |
| "Section 6 is empty, I will find something" | Then the session had no friction, and that is a data point. Inventing one poisons the count it feeds. |
| "I will quote the guilty sentence and say what it should say" | The quote is section 7 of the summary; what it should say is a finding in `audit.md`. Both exist — put each where it belongs. |
| "The audit found nothing, so there is nothing to write" | Write what you checked. An unstated clean check reads as a check nobody ran. |
| "I ran the tests earlier, they passed" | Earlier is not now and there have been edits. Run them, or record the claim as unverified. |
| "The subagent said it wrote the file" | Then the file exists and `git status` shows it. If you did not look, that is exactly the finding. |
| "This rule was bent for a good reason" | Then the reason is a finding, and it belongs where somebody can agree with it. |
| "I know why that script refused" | Do you, in this session? If you did not read it, mark the cause a hypothesis and name the file. |
| "I will fix this small thing while I am here" | Then the audit cannot be checked and the fix arrives unreviewed. Report it. |
| "`git add spec/changes/<CR>/` is simpler" | It is how a half-written archive got committed once already. Use `commit`. |
| "Capture warned about size, I will pass `--force`" | `--force` is for a source that shrank, not for a repository that grew. Say the number to the user. |
| "There is no change record but this session mattered" | Hard stop. Archive into the change this work belonged to, from its branch. |
</common_rationalizations>

<integration>

### Tools used
`Bash` for the five verbs and for the falsifying commands. `Write` for the two documents.
`Read`, `Grep` and `Glob` only for what a specific discrepancy needs. `AskUserQuestion` when
the capture reports an unusual size or personal-data shapes.

`spec/changes/<CR>/sessions/<session-id>/` — `transcript.jsonl`, `sidecar/` and
`manifest.json` written by the script; `summary.md` and the judgement half of `audit.md`
written by you. Committed, because the point is that it outlives both the session and Claude
Code's own retention.

### Consumers
A human, later, across many sessions — through `sdd-retro round` and the prompt in
`/Users/jaroslawwasowski/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/retro-prompts/`.

**And the pipeline itself, which now depends on this skill.** That sentence used to read
